one_liner: Small embeddable C HTTP/1.1 server library on libev for embedded Linux; one first-party wrk run shows 1.74x nginx req/s.
what_it_does: A C library that adds an HTTP/HTTPS server to your own program, aimed at OpenWrt and other embedded Linux targets. You create a uh_server on a libev loop, call listen(), set a docroot and register path handlers (prefix ^, suffix $ or substring matches) that build responses through function pointers on uh_connection (send_head, send_header, end_headers, send, printf, end_response). Built-in handlers serve static files with range and conditional requests, CGI, uploads and dlopen plugins. It is a library you program, not a configurable server like nginx.
how_it_is_fast: Each worker is one libev event loop with non-blocking accept4() sockets. Requests are parsed by the callback-driven nodejs http-parser, which stores header and URL offsets into the connection's read buffer instead of copying them. Responses are printf'd into a per-connection write buffer; files over 2 KB go out with sendfile() and smaller ones are read into the buffer. Multi-core scaling comes from nginx-style pre-forked worker processes, either sharing one listening socket or each with its own SO_REUSEPORT listener.
when_to_use: OpenWrt or embedded Linux devices that need a web UI or REST endpoint inside an existing C daemon (opkg packages libuhttpd and libuhttpd-nossl exist)
Programs that already run a libev loop and want HTTP handlers on it without a separate server process
Small static files plus CGI or C handlers at modest concurrency, where a few hundred KB of library beats shipping nginx
TLS on constrained targets, where mbedTLS or wolfSSL are supported backends next to OpenSSL
when_not_to_use: As an nginx replacement: no config file, reverse proxy, caching, HTTP/2 or virtual hosts; the features list names HTTP/1.1, CGI, plugins, ranges and uploads only
Throughput-critical public services: the only evidence is one 2021 localhost wrk run against an nginx of unknown version and configuration
Non-Linux platforms: the code relies on accept4, sendfile from sys/sendfile.h, SO_REUSEPORT and prctl (examples)

Long-term security-sensitive deployments: it depends on the nodejs http-parser, whose upstream says it is not actively maintained (llhttp is its successor), and the project itself is stale (last code change 2025-08-08)
Requests with 50 or more headers (UHTTPD_MAX_HEADER_NUM 50 is a compile-time limit) or idle connections that need more than the fixed 30 s timeout

integration.form: shared lib by default; static lib with -DBUILD_STATIC=ON
integration.dependencies: libev; git submodules nodejs/http-parser, zhaojh329/buffer, zhaojh329/log and zhaojh329/ssl; optional OpenSSL, mbedTLS (3.x since 3.14.2) or wolfSSL; libdl for plugins
integration.min_toolchain: C (gnu99) with CMake 3.5+; builds with -O (that is, -O1) and -Werror by default (BUILD_WERROR option)
integration.platforms: Linux only, including OpenWrt cross builds
integration.thread_safety: not documented; each uh_server runs on one libev loop and scaling is by forked processes, not threads

gotchas: Harness flaw: the README Benchmark section (added 2021-01-03, commit 8070cc2) shows one 10 s wrk run per server and does not say which libuhttpd binary or how many processes ran, nor the nginx version, worker count or access_log setting. nginx's stock config logs every request, while libuhttpd's examples log nothing below LOG_ERR; with the README's '-v' run example they would log two lines per request. At about 249 bytes per nginx response versus 203 for libuhttpd (wrk binary units), test.html must be tiny, so the run measures per-request overhead, not file serving.

Bug in the file handler (src/file.c __serve_file): files of 2 KB or less are read with 'while (len) len -= buffer_put_fd(...)'. buffer_put_fd returns 0 at EOF and -1 on a read error, so a file that shrinks between stat() and read(), or a read error, spins that loop forever and hangs the whole event loop. This matters for status files in /tmp that are rewritten on embedded devices.

Bug in the multi-process examples (example/multi_process_server.c and multi_process_server_reuseport.c): they keep worker PIDs in pid_t workers[MAX_WORKER=10], but the worker count defaults to get_nprocs() and -w is unchecked, so on hosts with 12 or more CPUs (11 or more for the reuseport variant) the fork loop writes past the stack array.

Open build issues (#18 nossl not compiling, #25 cmake error) and -Werror on by default can break builds on newer compilers; pass -DBUILD_WERROR=OFF. A report of random 5-22 s stalls behind an nginx HTTPS reverse proxy (#28) was closed as not planned.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over Kore, Lwan or Sogou Workflow when the target is an OpenWrt or embedded Linux C program that needs a small embeddable HTTP/1.1 server on its existing libev loop. For server-class throughput, Kore (best-of-four wrk runs against nginx) and Lwan (TechEmpower results) have stronger evidence and more features.
verified_claims_summary: One first-party wrk -t4 -c400 -d10s run per server over localhost fetching test.html: libuhttpd on port 8080 did 281,328.83 req/s (2.12 ms average latency) against nginx on port 80 at 161,390.39 req/s (3.54 ms), about 1.74x (derived from page data). No compiler or flags, CPU, kernel, nginx version or configuration, libuhttpd version, server binary or process count is given, and responses differed in size (about 249 vs 203 bytes).
status_note: Stale but usable: release 3.14.2 (2024-10-26), last commit a CMake 4 compatibility fix merged 2025-08-08, MIT-licensed, small and packaged for OpenWrt; issues get sporadic answers, and the bundled http-parser is unmaintained upstream.
